title: KBD Hooks Config
description: User-configurable hooks fired around KBD lifecycle boundaries (phase, child, plan, execute, reflect, task, assess). Place this file at .kbd-orchestrator/hooks-config.json in your project. See kbd-process-orchestrator/SKILL.md → 'Hooks' for the canonical event taxonomy, payload, and override semantics.

description.description: Optional human-readable description of this config file

hooks.description: List of hook entries. Each entry fires when its event pattern matches the current step and event.

id.description: Unique identifier for this hook entry (used in log output)

description.description: Human-readable description of what this hook does

event.description: Event pattern in canonical form '<kind>:<edge>' where kind is one of: phase | child | plan | execute | reflect | task | assess | * and edge is one of: before | after | *. Examples: 'phase:before', 'task:after', 'reflect:*', '*:*'. Legacy aliases accepted for backward compatibility: snake_case names (on_phase_complete, on_plan_complete, on_reflection_complete, on_assessment_complete, on_change_complete, on_blocker_detected, on_cross_tool_handoff) and '<kind>:begin' / '<kind>:end' (mapped to 'before'/'after').

mode.description: augment (default): this hook fires alongside other hooks matching the same event. override: this hook replaces the built-in default reporter for matching dispatch points; at most one override per (kind, edge) resolves — project > user > builtin precedence, last-wins within a layer.

enabled.description: Set false to disable this hook without removing it

type.description: Action type. Currently only 'command' (shell) is supported.

command.description: Shell command to run. Variable substitution is supported for the following env vars: ${PHASE}, ${STEP}, ${EVENT}, ${KBD_PROJECT_NAME}, ${KBD_PROJECT_ROOT}, ${CHANGES_TOTAL}, ${CHANGES_COMPLETED}, ${LAST_UPDATED_BY}, ${TIMESTAMP}. All other environment variables from the shell session are also available.

timeout.description: Maximum seconds to wait for the command to complete. Commands that exceed this are killed and reported as timed-out.

on_failure.description: warn: print a warning and continue (default) | error: print error and exit with code 1 (blocks the hook script) | ignore: silently continue on non-zero exit
